Interchange type: test each option with BODMAS. The correct swap usually makes a ÷ come out whole (the 'clean-division tell': 2499÷17=147).
Coded-meaning type: rewrite the WHOLE expression with real operators first, then BODMAS. Never compute mid-rewrite.
Speed: last-digit attack — often only the units digit separates the options.
Word: name the relation in ≤3 words BEFORE looking at options. Trap: part-vs-function (bulb fits a socket, but runs on electricity).
Letter: convert first pair to A1–Z26, find the shift pattern, apply.
Number: test n²±k / n³±k first; with two pairs given, verify on both.
Split multi-letter terms into per-position columns; each column is usually a simple ±n.
Expect wrap-around (Z→A / A→Z) — the #1 error spot.
Blank-filling: look for count patterns (e.g. runs of 3,2,1).
Letter codes: test Atbash first (pair sums = 27). If it fails, reverse the word, then Atbash. Then ±n.
Number codes: sum A1–Z26 positions; watch for digit reversal (39→93).
Sentence codes: align sentences and cancel — common word takes the common code.
Write differences FIRST, always — then differences of differences. Catches ±n, n², ×n±k, primes.
Relations: test +,−,×,÷ between numbers; use the second example to kill wrong rules.
Never break numbers into digits — SSC explicitly forbids it.
Odd one out: check category, then spelling/letter-count, then arithmetic property — in that order.
Syllogism: draw Venn circles; 'Some A are B' never implies 'All'. Test each conclusion separately.
Seating: fix one person's position first, then place the rest relative to them.
Blood relations: draw the family tree top-down; solve from the known end.
Direction sense: draw the compass path step by step; final displacement via Pythagoras.
Mirror/water images: mirror flips left–right; water flips top–bottom.
